prompt:
You maintain a running summary of a long engineering document that is being read part by part, so that a later reader can model the system in SysML v2 without seeing the earlier parts.
Update the summary with the new part. Keep, as compactly as possible: the full names of system elements, actors and items; every alias or call sign with the full name it stands for; which element produces, sends or receives which item; modes and normative requirements. At most 300 words.

Current summary:
Scope: offshore-wind acceptance/O&M/refurbishment/decommissioning; excludes external grid/unrelated ports; reporting boundary active. Aliases: Glassfin=Turbine Controller; Morrowick=Offshore Substation; Pale Lantern=Weather Service; Juniper Vale=SCADA Gateway; Thistle Crown=Maintenance Planning Engine; Amber Quay=Shore Control Room; Kestrel Bay=Crew Transfer Vessel; Sable Orchard=Fleet Dispatch Console; Mosslight=Warehouse System; Copper Finch=Metocean Buoy; Quiet Harbor=Cybersecurity Gateway; Blue Granite=Vessel AIS Receiver; Larkspur=Blade Inspection Drone; Redoubt=Work Permit Portal; Foxglove=Emergency Generator; Wildmere=Grid Interface Relay. Elements: Pitch System; Converter Cabinet; Nacelle Condition Monitor; Rotor Brake Unit; Turbine Sensor Bus; Main Transformer; Export Cable Monitor; Daughter Craft; Service Operations Vessel; Helideck; North Access Scanner; South Access Scanner; Personnel Tracking Console; Spares Hub; Operations Radio Console. Actors: SCADA Engineer; technical reviewers; Electrical Technician; Control Engineer; Grid Dispatcher; Substation Operator; Blade Specialist; Field Supervisor; Marine Coordinator; Duty Planner; Vessel Master; Weather Analyst; Storekeeper; Port Agent; Rescue Coordinator; HSE Officer. Flows: Glassfin→Pitch Deviation Notice; Blue Granite→Position Quality Flag→Sable Orchard; Duty Planner→Transfer Manifest Addendum; Mosslight→Backorder Exception Slip→Storekeeper/part-validation; Copper Finch→Wave Burst Record→Pale Lantern→Squall Window Bulletin→Thistle Crown; Juniper Vale→Session Revocation Receipt/alarms/status→Amber Quay; HSE Officer→Harness Audit Card; Morrowick→Transformer Tap Snapshot on requested review. Requirements: Duty Planner confirms technical basis/feasibility; safety/substantial-loss faults outrank inspections; due-date/condition/value justify outages. Monitors/bus/Larkspur inform planning; Field Supervisor validates faults/offshore necessity. Forecast-confidence, vessel-capability/transit/worksite-limits govern access selection; Weather Hold blocks limit-exceeding mobilization. Sable Orchard assigns vessels/crews after priority-confirmation; Marine Coordinator coordinates changes. Commitment requires parts/competence/duration; schedule long-lead work early. Redoubt checks controlled-access/isolation readiness; HSE Officer verifies controls; Substation Operator confirms constraints. Scanners authorize-entry records; Personnel Tracking Console tracks roster/returns; Amber Quay oversees

New part:
S269: The Duty Planner revises priorities when asset condition, access forecasts, or resource availability changes, and communicates the resulting plan to affected teams.
S270: Weather Service provides forecast conditions and confidence information for planned work areas and vessel routes.
S271: Metocean Buoy observations give the team a local reference for checking forecast trends and current sea state.
S272: Weather Analyst compares forecast data with recent observations before advising on the reliability of a work window.
S273: Forecast confidence is considered alongside the predicted conditions rather than treated as a substitute for operational limits.
S274: The Duty Planner checks that the expected conditions remain within the limits for the task, transfer method, and vessel.
S275: Low confidence near a limit leads to more conservative planning and a shorter review interval.
S276: A Weather Hold is applied when conditions are outside the approved limits or the available evidence is insufficient to support safe work.
S277: The Marine Coordinator reviews access options and vessel availability when a work window narrows.
S278: The Vessel Master receives the Transfer Manifest Addendum before departure.
S279: The Crew Transfer Vessel proceeds only when the Vessel Master considers the approach and transfer conditions acceptable.
S280: A forecast that improves does not by itself release a hold, because the team also checks current observations and the task-specific limits.
S281: The Service Operations Vessel may provide a more stable work platform, but its operating limits still govern whether work can proceed.
S282: Vessel Standby is used when transit or station keeping remains possible but personnel transfer or task execution is not justified.
S283: The Marine Coordinator reassesses the route when wind direction, wave conditions, or visibility changes materially.
S284: The Vessel Master can pause or abort an approach when observed conditions differ from the forecast or deteriorate during transit.
S285: Maintenance Planning Engine produces the Deferred Task Rationale when weather prevents a planned task from proceeding.
S286: The rationale supports later reprioritization without implying that the task is safe under the current conditions.
S287: Quiet Harbor blocks a route change when the required authorization is incomplete.
S288: Blue Granite provides vessel position information for review against the planned route and operating area.
S289: The team considers forecast uncertainty when deciding whether to commit crews, fuel, and vessel time to a remote work site.
S290: When conditions are changing rapidly, the Marine Coordinator seeks an updated forecast before confirming a departure or transfer plan.

Return JSON {"summary": "..."}.
